 Hyundai’s Non-OEM Parts Position, BMW’s Park-Outside Water Pump Recall, and Toyota’s Takata Airbag Recall 
 An automaker revises its parts sourcing stance as two recalls top 1 million vehicles.
 Jess Fritsche 
 Nov 17, 2026 
 Read Time: 
 2 Mins 
 News 
 Recalls 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Share on LinkedIn 
 Share by email 
 Hyundai Motor America’s revised position statement says the automaker does not approve of non-original parts for collision repairs. 
 Key takeaways 
 Hyundai revises its non-OEM parts position statement 
 BMW reissues water pump fire recall with a park-outside advisory 
 Toyota recalls 314,000 vehicles for Takata passenger airbag inflators 
 Hyundai revises its non-OEM parts position statement
 Hyundai Motor America has posted a revised position statement on non-original collision parts, dated Nov. 6 in its OEM1Stop filename. The statement says Hyundai “does not approve” of counterfeit, gray market, aftermarket, imitation, recycled, alternate, or other non-original parts for collision repairs. It extends that to components pulled from another collision-damaged vehicle.
 For post-collision repairs that may affect occupant safety, Hyundai “requires that dealers use Hyundai Genuine Parts or demonstrate that the parts used are equivalent in quality and design.” The statement adds that Hyundai has stepped up brand protection through its partnership with Mobis Parts America. It does not say what changed from the prior version.
 BMW reissues water pump fire recall with a park-outside advisory
 BMW of North America is recalling 720,796 vehicles because degradation at the water pump’s electrical connector could let moisture into the pump and cause a short circuit. That’s according to a Part 573 Safety Recall Report filed Nov. 4 with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The filing covers 2012–2018 models, including the 3 Series, 5 Series, X1, and X3.
 The same vehicles were recalled over the water pump in 2024 under campaign 24V608. BMW’s report says pumps returned from vehicles that had received the 2024 remedy showed brittleness in the connector’s plastic, though the filing does not name a root cause. NHTSA said BMW knows of roughly 10 U.S. incidents that “relate, or may relate” to the issue, all in vehicles repaired under the earlier recall. The new remedy under campaign 26V733 is still in development, and owners are advised to park outdoors until the repair is done, keeping clear of buildings and other vehicles.
 Toyota recalls 314,000 vehicles for Takata passenger airbag inflators
 Toyota Motor North America announced Nov. 12 a voluntary recall of about 314,000 Toyota and Lexus vehicles in the U.S. equipped with Takata-made front passenger airbags. Over time, the inflator’s propellant can break down in certain heat and humidity conditions, the automaker said. If the airbag then deploys, the inflator can rupture and may send metal fragments into the cabin.
 Depending on the model, dealers will install either a new front passenger inflator or a complete airbag assembly, free to owners. The U.S. release names no models. A companion Toyota Canada release lists 2003–2008 Corolla, 2005–2007 Sequoia, 2016–2017 4Runner, and 2017 Lexus GX460 vehicles among those affected in that country. As of Nov. 17, NHTSA’s recall database showed no matching campaign for those models.
